post.author: Christofer Dutz
post.topic_summary: Acquired a Mitsubishi Q03UDECPU to build Mitsubishi protocol drivers for ToddySoft GmbH, possibly contributing to Apache PLC4X if community helps.

comment_posted.comment_text:
The Q03UDECPU's built-in Ethernet runs MC Protocol (3E frame, TCP, port 5007). That part is relatively well-documented. The harder part of the Q-series landscape is that many production installs on automotive and packaging lines still use older Q02/Q06 CPUs with a QJ71E71-100 Ethernet module added later: those add the network/station/unit addressing layer the driver has to account for.

The other thing that tends to surface in field deployments: a lot of the process data plants actually want to collect lives in CC-Link remote stations rather than the main CPU registers. MC Protocol gets you the CPU data space fine, but cycle counters and analog values on remote I/O heads are a separate protocol path entirely. That distinction usually appears after the driver is working and the plant engineer says the number they want is on the remote head.
